title: Directive auto-close can never close a propose-only authoring-directive — 'proposed' is absent from the terminal whitelist, so DIRECTIVE-001/-003-class commissions are structurally zombie-pending forever. Add a per-directive opt-in that treats the linked propose-only PROP reaching 'proposed' as terminal-for-the-directive.
directive_note: Authored during the Candidate-A (PROP/directive-graph archaeology) lane while reconciling the 06-28 deep-dive directive lifecycle. This is the highest-signal OBE-not-marked finding the graph walk surfaced. NOT a full Candidate-A deliverable — Candidate A's full ~115-PROP dependency-graph walk remains for the next run once DIRECTIVE-20260628-004's own gate (003 marked completed, done this run) clears.
why_human_needed: Changes the directive auto-close trust graph (PROP-108). Loosening the terminal whitelist — even behind a per-directive opt-in — risks closing a directive whose propose-only PROP was authored but then rejected/superseded by the operator. Operator must approve the opt-in semantics and decide whether to also flip directive-auto-close-enforce.flag.
do_not_auto_close_reason: propose-only + requires_human_judgment; and self-referentially, this PROP's own deliverable is a propose-only PROP — it cannot satisfy the very whitelist it is trying to fix. That recursion IS the bug.
problem_statement: The PROP-108 directive auto-close (Pre-flight: Directive Lifecycle Auto-Close in tinker.md) closes a pending directive only when its linked PROP.status is in the conservative terminal whitelist {implemented, integrated, applied, self-applied, completed}. Many operator directives commission a PROPOSE-ONLY deliverable ('Author a propose-only PROP ...'). The deliverable PROP correctly terminates at status 'proposed' (it is never implemented — that is the point). 'proposed' is not in the whitelist, so these directives can NEVER auto-close. They sit status:pending forever, re-entering the dispatcher's Operator-Directive Discovery sort every single run.

zombie_directives_observed_this_run.reason: 'proposed' not terminal; deliverable is propose-only so it never will be
'integrated' IS terminal — directive-auto-close.js flagged it would-close in shadow this run

older_high_priority_zombies_same_class.note: phase-shipped, not in whitelist, HAS a directive_id back-ref. Partially OBE — deliverable shipped in shadow; enforce-mode toggle still pending. Operator judgment on whether to close.

PROP-113 carries NO directive_id / source_directive back-ref so auto-close linkage cannot resolve even if whitelist included phase-shipped. Same FND-03 pattern flagged in tinker report 2026-06-20 (PROP-091/092).

evidence.shadow_run_this_run: directive-auto-close.js (shadow) walked 116 directives, 24 pending, found exactly 1 would-close (DIRECTIVE-20260628-002 via PROP-117 integrated). It missed 001 and 003 BECAUSE their deliverables are propose-only ('proposed' not terminal), and missed 022/023-001 because PROP-113/114 lack back-refs. So the auto-close, even in enforce mode, would clear only 1 of the ~6 verifiable-OBE zombies.

two_distinct_root_causes.RC1_propose_only_never_terminal: An authoring-directive whose deliverable is a propose-only PROP has no reachable terminal PROP status. 'proposed' is the END state for that deliverable but the whitelist excludes it. Structural, not a data error.
two_distinct_root_causes.RC2_missing_back_refs: Shipped implementation PROPs (PROP-113, PROP-114) carry no directive_id/source_directive back-ref, so the forward-back-ref linkage path can't connect them to their commissioning directive. Recurrence of FND-03 from tinker-2026-06-20 (then PROP-091/092). The mark-directive-superseded.js backfill tool exists for exactly this but wasn't run for 113/114.

recommendation.primary_RC1_fix: Add an opt-in directive field `deliverable_is_propose_only: true` (or reuse a `auto_close_when_deliverable_proposed: true` flag mirroring the existing `auto_close_when_phase_0_done` opt-in). When present on a directive, directive-auto-close.js expands that directive's terminal whitelist to additionally accept linked-PROP.status === 'proposed'. Default behavior is UNCHANGED for implementation directives. Guard against the rejected-PROP edge: the opt-in should NOT fire if the linked PROP status indicates operator rejection (e.g. 'rejected','superseded','withdrawn'); only a bare 'proposed' counts.
recommendation.secondary_RC2_fix: Backfill directive_id back-refs on PROP-113 and PROP-114 (and audit the rest of the shipped corpus) so linkage resolves. Tool exists: `node monitor/scripts/mark-directive-superseded.js PROP-113 by DIRECTIVE-20260622-001` etc., OR add a plain `directive_id` field. Operator/next-run runs from a clone and pushes.
recommendation.tertiary_operator_toggle: Once RC1+RC2 land and a shadow run shows the expected would-close set, consider flipping `monitor/decisions/directive-auto-close-enforce.flag` to enforce so the backlog drains mechanically each run instead of needing manual flips.
recommendation.interim_manual_action_taken_this_run: This run manually flipped DIRECTIVE-20260628-001,-002,-003 to status:completed (clone-write+push, additive-edit per CLAUDE.md DIRECTIVE-LIFECYCLE exception) because all three are 100%-verified OBE (PROP-116 authored, PROP-117 integrated, PROP-119 authored). This unblocks DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 (Candidate A) whose gate is '003 marked completed'. The older highs (019/022/023-001) were NOT auto-flipped — left for operator confirmation since their phase-shipped statuses are ambiguous about full-intent completion.

the_other_side_arguments: AGAINST RC1 fix: loosening the whitelist (even per-directive) is exactly the conservatism PROP-108 was designed to preserve; a propose-only PROP can be authored and then REJECTED by the operator, and auto-closing its directive on 'proposed' would mark the commission done while its output is being thrown away. Counter: the opt-in is per-directive (operator sets it knowingly when filing a propose-only commission), and the rejected/superseded guard prevents closing on a killed PROP. Net risk low and bounded.

AGAINST acting at all: only ~3-6 directives are affected and a human can flip them in seconds; building machinery for a 6-item backlog is over-engineering. Counter: the backlog is not static — every propose-only commission (and the operator files them regularly during quiet periods) becomes a permanent zombie that re-enters the dispatcher sort on the single most expensive agent (tinker) every run. The fix is ~15 lines in directive-auto-close.js.

AGAINST the manual flips this run: tinker unilaterally marking 3 directives completed is a write into the operator-directive surface; if my OBE judgment were wrong, work could be silently dropped. Counter: all three deliverables were directly read and verified terminal; the flips are additive-only (status pending->completed + metadata) per the documented exception; and the conservative older-zombie set was deliberately left untouched.

AGAINST RC2 framing: maybe PROP-113/114 SHOULDN'T carry directive back-refs if authored independently and only incidentally satisfy a directive. Counter: DIRECTIVE-022/023-001 explicitly commission 'PROP-113 full design' / 'PROP-114 full design' by name — the back-ref is factually correct and its absence is an omission.
scope_discipline_note: This run did NOT execute the full Candidate-A PROP-dependency-graph walk (all ~115 PROPs: supersedes/superseded_by/amends/depends_on edges, broken-link detection, wrongly-marked verification_pattern audit). That remains DIRECTIVE-20260628-004's deliverable for the NEXT tinker run, now unblocked (003 marked completed this run). PROP-120 captures the single highest-signal finding the partial walk surfaced — the propose-only terminal gap — because it explains the entire visible zombie backlog and is independently actionable.
